title: Government budget by sector, Kenya
basis: The figures are the ten sector ceilings printed in Table 3.2 of the 2026 Budget Policy Statement (The National Treasury and Economic Planning, February 2026), in KSh million, for two financial years: the approved budget for FY 2025/26 and the projected ceiling for FY 2026/27, each split into recurrent gross and development gross as the table prints them. Both columns are estimates: the FY 2025/26 column is the approved budget position as restated in February 2026, and the FY 2026/27 column is a projection published before appropriation. Neither is an actual outturn, and no outturn figure appears in this file. A third view carries the original FY 2025/26 ceilings as first published in the February 2025 Budget Policy Statement, so the original estimate and the later approved position can be seen side by side without being mixed.

conventions.page_numbers: Page references are the page of the PDF file at the source URL, and the printed page number is given where the document prints one. The two differ by the front matter.
conventions.three_facts_kept_apart: An ORIGINAL estimate (the ceiling first published in the Budget Policy Statement before the budget was appropriated), an APPROVED budget (the position as restated in the following year's Budget Policy Statement, which may already include in-year revisions), and an ACTUAL outturn are three different facts. This file carries the first two only. No outturn figure is present anywhere in it.
conventions.no_outturn: A per-sector outturn for FY2025/26 was not found in a primary document within this task. The 2026 Budget Review and Outlook Paper publishes FY2025/26 outturn in aggregate, not by sector. The sector lines here are therefore all estimates of one kind or another, and each record says which kind.
conventions.recurrent_and_development: Recurrent gross and development gross are the two rows the National Treasury prints under each sector subtotal in Table 3.2. They are kept as printed. A blank means the document does not print it, never that it is zero.
conventions.units: KSh million in the Table 3.2 views. The FY2025/26 original ceiling view was published in KSh billion to one decimal and has been multiplied by 1,000 to sit in the same unit; as_published keeps the printed form.
conventions.coverage: The ten sector ceilings are national government ministerial ceilings grouped by sector working group. They do not include debt service, the equitable share to county governments, the contingency fund or the Equalization Fund, so the ten do not add to the total budget. The reconciliation block states both numbers and does not assert that the difference is fully explained.

reconciliation.stated_difference: The ten sector ceilings total KSh 2,867,422.5 million against a projected total budget of KSh 4,737,500 million, a gap of KSh 1,870,077.5 million. That gap is NOT allocated to a sector and is NOT a residual explained by the outside-ceiling items: public debt related costs of KSh 1,542,100 million plus transfers to counties of KSh 495,500 million plus the contingency fund of KSh 2,000 million come to KSh 2,039,600 million, which is larger than the gap by KSh 169,522.5 million. The two tables have different coverage, the Budget Policy Statement publishes no reconciliation between them, and the difference is therefore printed by the checker and left open rather than forced to balance.
reconciliation.check: The difference is printed by the checker and is not asserted to be equal to the sum of the outside-ceiling items.

not_sourced: Actual outturn by sector for any financial year. Not found in a primary Treasury document within this task.

Supplementary estimates by sector for FY2025/26. The approved budget column in Table 3.2 may already reflect in-year revisions, but the BPS does not say which, so no supplementary revision is recorded.
Sector figures for the FY2026/27 Appropriation Act. The Act itself was not read in this task, so the appropriated figures, which may differ from the BPS projection, are absent rather than inferred.
notes: The 2026 Budget Policy Statement paragraph 291 states the PAIR allocation for FY2026/27 as KSh 367.5 billion while paragraph 292 and Table 3.2 both state KSh 354.9 billion. The table figure is used and the paragraph 292 figure agrees with it.

Table 3.2 internal arithmetic: recurrent gross plus development gross equals the printed subtotal for all ten sectors to within 0.1 KSh million in three cases, and the ten subtotals add to the printed grand total exactly for FY2025/26 and to within 0.1 for FY2026/27. Both checks are re-run by the checker.

The Kenya Revenue Authority, the National Treasury itself and the public debt service do not appear as separate sectors in Table 3.2 because debt service is a first charge outside the sector ceilings.

The two FY2025/26 views disagree for several sectors, which is why they are kept apart. Health is KSh 204.5 billion as the original February 2025 ceiling and KSh 138.1 billion as the approved budget restated in February 2026; EII is KSh 504.6 billion and KSh 534.6 billion. The aggregate is almost unchanged (KSh 2,562.1 billion against KSh 2,549.5 billion), so the movement is between sectors and not a change in the total. Neither document explains the revision, and this file does not reconcile them.
